title: *PSY405 GDB Solution*
text:
*PSY405 GDB Solution*

In the light of Sigmund Freud's psychoanalytic theory, I strongly believe that personality is largely the product of *early life experiences* rather than just heredity.

Freud explained that human personality is built around Id, Ego and Superego, and this structure is formed during the first 6 years of life through psychosexual stages. Any unresolved conflict during these stages creates a fixation which later appears as a stable personality trait.

To justify my stance, I would give two points:

First, our upbringing defines our traits. For example, Freud noted that a child who experiences overly strict or harsh parenting during the anal stage (toilet training period) often grows up to be extremely organized, rigid and obsessed with perfection. This type of anal personality is not inherited, it is developed due to early handling.

Second, inherited factors only provide a general tendency. We may get a temperament like being sensitive or energetic from our parents, but how it will be expressed depends on environment. For example, two children can inherit introversion, but the one raised with encouragement and love may become a calm and focused adult, while the other raised with rejection and criticism may develop social withdrawal and anxiety. The genetic base was same, but the childhood experience made the difference.

To conclude, heredity gives us the blueprint, but it is early childhood that actually constructs the building of personality.
